title: Working in an office
subtitle: photocopier, paperwork, run out of
summary: Name the things in an office, describe the work people do there, and talk about the problems of a bad day.

lesson.heading: Office equipment
rows: a machine that makes copies of documents
a machine that prints documents from a computer
the part of a computer with the letter keys on it
a tall piece of furniture where you keep **files**
a board on the wall where you put messages and information
something on the wall that tells you the date
a book where you write down appointments and things you have to do
a small machine that adds up numbers and does maths
the place where you throw away paper you don't want

lesson.heading: Office work
lesson.text: Josh works for a company which **produces** furniture. He doesn't work in the factory where the furniture is made, but in the offices across the road. His job **involves** quite a lot of **paperwork**: work that uses paper, e.g. reports and forms.

examples.text: His job **involves** quite a lot of paperwork.

examples.note: an invoice shows how much the customer has to pay

lesson.heading: arrange, attend and organise
lesson.text: Josh has to **arrange** (plan and prepare) visits to other companies and **make appointments** for his boss. Sometimes he **shows visitors round** the factory, and occasionally he has to **attend** meetings.

examples.text: He has to **arrange** visits to other companies.

examples.note: an appointment is an arranged time when you meet someone
attend is formal; in everyday English we say go to

examples.text: One of his most important tasks is to **organise** the office party every year.

lesson.heading: Office problems
lesson.text: Josh is having a bad day. When a machine stops working, it **breaks down**. When there is no more of something, you have **run out of** it. The people you work with are your **colleagues**.

examples.text: The printer **has run out of** paper.

examples.note: absent = not in the office; in everyday English we say off

examples.text: There is **loads of** work to do.

lesson.text: A machine *breaks down*, but you *run out of* the things it uses - paper, ink, coffee.

exercises.prompt: I threw all that old paper in the rubbish ___.
exercises.explanation: A rubbish bin is the place where you throw away paper you don't want.

exercises.prompt: He put most of the documents in the filing ___.
exercises.explanation: A filing cabinet is where you keep your files.

exercises.prompt: It's a very boring job and I spend most of my time doing general paper___.
exercises.explanation: Paperwork is work that uses paper, e.g. reports and forms.

exercises.prompt: I told him to put the details on the notice___.
exercises.explanation: A noticeboard is a board on the wall for messages and information.

exercises.prompt: Match each definition with the right office word.

pairs.left: Something on a wall which tells you the date
A book where you write down appointments
A paper showing what a customer must pay
A device that helps you do maths

exercises.prompt: *A:* What does the company do? *B:* It ___ electronic equipment.
exercises.explanation: To produce something means to make it.

exercises.prompt: *A:* I can't come on Friday. *B:* OK. Do you want me to make another ___ for you?
exercises.explanation: You make an appointment when you arrange a time to meet someone.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Why can't we use the printer? *B:* It's run ___ of ink.
exercises.explanation: To run out of something means to have no more of it.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Do you have to ___ meetings? *B:* Yes, sometimes, if my boss is away.
exercises.explanation: To attend a meeting is the formal way of saying to go to a meeting.

exercises.prompt: *A:* We've got some visitors coming tomorrow. *B:* Would you like me to show them ___ the factory?
exercises.explanation: To show someone round means to take them from place to place and explain things.

exercises.statement: 'My boss is off today' means the same as 'My boss is absent today'.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Off is the everyday word; absent is more formal.

exercises.prompt: 'The photocopier is broken.' Another way to say this is: The photocopier isn't ___.
exercises.explanation: When a machine stops working we say it isn't working or it has broken down.

exercises.prompt: Put each word in the right group.
Say that there is a lot of work today, using an informal phrase.
exercises.answer: We've got loads of work today.
exercises.explanation: Loads of is an informal way of saying lots of.
